divergences: CGNAT: ssrf_guard._ip_is_blocked additionally blocks RFC 6598 100.64.0.0/10 (IPv4Address only), applied verbatim from open/unmerged PR #630 (head ff070bd5e9dadeaa5da32ccffd868b15eb642aa9, which changes src/alienclaw/tools/_ssrf_guard.py a67f6c7d -> 328ac5f8). In-tree allows these addresses. It is one of three decision differences at equivalent configuration (the Azure WireServer and port-0 entries below are the others); tests/test_parity_in_tree.py asserts it explicitly and fails if in-tree starts blocking CGNAT.
test_url_fetch_ssrf_cgnat.py derives from PR #630 head ff070bd5; the file is absent at source_commit, so its source_blob is taken from that PR commit, not from source_commit.
boundary: removed the OpenClaw/env helpers workspace_root(), file_write_root(), _openclaw_home() and the _OPENCLAW_SUBPATH constant; callers always pass the boundary root explicitly.

boundary: the hardcoded ~/.openclaw denial inside assert_inside_boundary became a keyword-only parameter deny_roots=() (iterable of str/PathLike; a single str/PathLike is accepted). Default denies nothing beyond the boundary. With deny_roots=[Path.home() / '.openclaw'] every decision is identical to in-tree (asserted by tests/test_parity_in_tree.py).

boundary: deny-root rejection message changed from 'OpenClaw workspace denied: "<path>" targets an OpenClaw agent directory' to 'Denied root: "<path>" targets a denied directory'. All other error messages in both modules are byte-identical to in-tree.
Docstrings/comments genericised (product names, ticket numbers and caller file references removed).

2026-11-26: three security fixes were applied to BOTH sides (in-tree src/alienclaw/tools and this package) with identical code, so they are not divergences: (1) dotfile rule: the final component that names something is checked ('.env/', '.env/./' were accepted because basename() was ''), and so is the resolved path's final component (symlink to a dotfile); dot-directories stay allowed; (2) checked host vs connected host: the guard refuses backslash/whitespace/control characters, userinfo, '%' in the host, a second ':' outside brackets, host characters outside [a-z0-9._-] after IDNA, and any URL whose urllib/http.client (host, port) differs from the checked one, and it now RETURNS A CANONICAL URL (lower-case scheme/host, IDNA host, port only if given, no userinfo) instead of the input; covers security-review SR-01 (backslash with requests) and SR-03 (multi-colon port split, %2f/%23); (3) assert_no_symlink gained keyword-only operation='write' (message wording only) so read paths can use it; in-tree file_read now calls it on the unresolved path and opens with O_NOFOLLOW (file_read has no staged counterpart). The ssrf_guard/boundary source_blob values above are the FIXED in-tree blobs (uncommitted when written, so absent at source_commit); the CGNAT divergence is unchanged.

2026-11-26: tests/test_file_boundary.py and tests/test_http_get_ssrf.py had their strict xfails (trailing-slash dotfile; connect host) converted into passing regression tests; the in-tree tests they were adapted from are unchanged. tests/test_connect_host.py additionally checks the returned URL against urllib3, httpx and yarl (each skipped if not installed); that part has no in-tree counterpart. tests/test_parity_in_tree.py's corpus gained the new URL and path vectors.

Ported tests are guard-level only: tool-level assertions (RunResult ok/correctness, atomic write, output contract, compute/extract_json/search_text guards in test_file_boundary.py) were not ported. The real-socket HTTPServer redirect tests were replaced with an in-process urllib handler, and DNS is a fake resolver (real libc parser via AI_NUMERICHOST for literals), so the suite is network-free.

connection pinning added (staged only, 2026-11-26): new src/agent_tool_sandbox/pinning.py (resolve_and_validate -> PinnedTarget, build_pinned_opener, pinned_urlopen, PinnedHTTPConnection/PinnedHTTPSConnection: dial only the validated IPs, no second resolution, Host/SNI/cert check on the original host, no redirects, no proxies) and tests/test_pinning.py; __init__.py re-exports the four public names. In ssrf_guard.py the body of assert_safe_fetch_url moved into private _validate_fetch_url, which also returns scheme/host/effective port and the ONE resolution's addresses; assert_safe_fetch_url returns its canonical_url. Decisions and messages are unchanged (parity corpus unchanged and green). In-tree src/alienclaw/tools has no pinning.

2026-11-26 (review follow-up): assert_no_symlink fails closed when a path component cannot be inspected. Python 3.12's Path.is_symlink() re-raises lstat errors other than ENOENT/ENOTDIR/EBADF/ELOOP (EACCES under an unsearchable directory, e.g. /root/.ssh/id_rsa), so a caller catching only ValueError crashed; any OSError is now ValueError('Path not inspectable on <operation>: "<path>" (<reason>)'). Applied to BOTH sides with identical code and message (a new _is_symlink helper), so it is not a divergence. tests/test_uninspectable_path.py is the guard-level part of the in-tree test/tools/test_boundary_uninspectable_path.py. The in-tree test/tools/test_ssrf_guard_connect_host.py changed only in its tool-level test (output url is the caller's input, the new fetched_url is the canonical URL), which is not ported, so tests/test_connect_host.py is unchanged and only its source_blob was refreshed.

Azure WireServer (staged only, 2026-11-26; shared vector corpus meta-azure-wireserver): ssrf_guard._ip_is_blocked additionally blocks the single public address 168.63.129.16 (new _METADATA_IPS frozenset, IPv4Address only like CGNAT; _resolve_host_ips and pinning._checked_addresses unwrap IPv4-mapped answers first, and 6to4/Teredo/NAT64 embeddings were already blocked as ranges). Refusal message is the existing 'Refusing blocked IP 168.63.129.16 (resolved from ...)'. In-tree allows it. A DECISION divergence, declared in tests/test_parity_in_tree.py (WIRESERVER_DIVERGENT_URLS, the IP corpus and test_wireserver_divergence_is_one_address_and_it_is_real), which fails if in-tree starts blocking it.

Port 0 (staged only, 2026-11-26; shared vector corpus port-zero): _validate_fetch_url refuses an explicit port outside 1-65535 right after parsing it, with 'Refusing URL with port 0: ports must be 1-65535' (urlparse already raises for ports above 65535, so in practice only 0 is new). In-tree returns the URL unchanged. A DECISION divergence, declared in tests/test_parity_in_tree.py (PORT_ZERO_DIVERGENT_URLS, test_port_zero_divergence_is_port_zero_only). pinning.py is unchanged: resolve_and_validate goes through _validate_fetch_url.

tests/test_wireserver_port_zero.py is new (no in-tree counterpart): regression tests for the two entries above plus pins for the 6to4, Teredo, fec0::/10 and NAT64-WireServer blocks this package already had and the TS package now matches.

Total deadline (staged only, 2026-11-26; PINNING-SECURITY-REVIEW PR-02, plan gate G4): pinned_urlopen's timeout is now ONE time.monotonic() budget for the resolution, every connect attempt (each gets what is left), TLS, sending (re-armed per 16 KiB), the response head and every read of the returned response, across redirect hops; it raises the new pinning.DeadlineExceededError (a TimeoutError and a urllib.error.URLError, with .phase). Under a deadline the one resolution runs in a daemon thread (getaddrinfo cannot be interrupted), at most 16 at once, abandoned ones included; past the cap a call fails closed. timeout must be None or a positive finite number (ValueError/TypeError). build_pinned_opener and PinnedHTTP(S)Connection gained keyword deadline=None (unchanged per-operation behaviour without it). No in-tree counterpart. Tests: tests/test_deadline.py; tests/test_pinning.py test_timeout_reaches_the_socket / test_default_timeout_is_bounded now expect the remaining budget (<= timeout) instead of timeout itself.

Refusal messages (staged only, 2026-11-26; PR-03): a refusal that depends on the DNS answer no longer names the resolved address and reads the same for blocked and unresolvable: "Refusing hostname '<host>': not an allowed destination". SsrfBlockedError (still a ValueError) gained keyword-only detail (the reference message, e.g. 'Refusing blocked IP 10.0.0.1 (resolved from ...)'; equal to str(exc) when nothing is withheld), blocked_address and hostname. A MESSAGE divergence, declared in tests/test_parity_in_tree.py (decisions and reference messages compared through exc.detail; test_refusal_message_divergence). Tests: tests/test_refusal_disclosure.py; tests/test_pinning.py and tests/test_wireserver_port_zero.py assert the detail instead of the old text.

Loopback names and redaction (staged only, 2026-11-26; plan gate G7): _validate_fetch_url refuses localhost, *.localhost (trailing dots too) and ip6-localhost/ip6-loopback after IDNA and before DNS (RFC 6761 §6.3), 'Refusing hostname <host>: reserved loopback name (RFC 6761)'; in-tree refuses them only through a loopback answer. Shared corpus: loc-localhost-lying-resolver python allow -> block (now equal to ts). Every URL that goes into a message (redirect Location, the pinned-to and inconsistent-target messages, malformed-URL text from urllib/http.client) has its userinfo, query and fragment replaced by REDACTED (_redact_url, _scrub). Declared in tests/test_parity_in_tree.py (LOOPBACK_NAME_URLS). Tests: tests/test_localhost_and_redaction.py.

Opt-in redirects (staged only, 2026-11-26; plan gate G5): pinned_urlopen(follow_redirects=0) keeps refusing every 301/302/303/307/308 with the same message; with N in 1..20 each hop is re-validated and re-pinned (its own resolution), https -> http is refused, Authorization, Cookie, Proxy-Authorization and a caller-set Host are dropped on a cross-origin hop, 307/308 keep method and body, 301/302/303 become a body-less GET (HEAD stays HEAD), the redirect body is never read, and hops share the total deadline. build_pinned_opener is unchanged (still refuses redirects). Tests: tests/test_redirects.py.

Data-driven block list (staged only, 2026-11-26; prepares plan gate G3, no decision change): _ip_is_blocked and _is_loopback_name read the new GENERATED module src/agent_tool_sandbox/_blocklist_data.py (written by ../policy/gen_python.py from ../policy/blocklist.v1.json, the table the TS package reads too) instead of the ipaddress.is_* properties, _CGNAT_NETWORK, _METADATA_IPS and _LOOPBACK_NAMES (all three constants removed). Every range is enumerated explicitly; IPv4-mapped and NAT64 are named matchers (block whole / decode the low 32 bits / defer). _resolve_host_ips unwraps IPv4-mapped answers only while the table's ipv4-mapped matcher is a decode (UNWRAP_IPV4_MAPPED, true today). Zero behaviour change on CPython 3.10.22/3.11.17/3.12.13/3.14.9: all 296 shared-corpus verdicts and messages identical, the parity corpus unchanged, and an old-vs-new differential over ~600k addresses per interpreter agreed everywhere; a raw IPv4-mapped IPv6Address handed straight to _ip_is_blocked still skips CGNAT and WireServer (decode_excludes), as in-tree does. On older unpatched interpreters the table's verdicts now apply instead of that interpreter's ipaddress tables. Tests: tests/test_blocklist_data.py (byte-for-byte drift check of the generated module, no is_* attribute in ssrf_guard.py, profile semantics, schema refusals).

Redirect fixes from the shared redirect corpus (staged only, 2026-11-26; plan gate G5): pinned_urlopen reads a non-ASCII Location's bytes as UTF-8 (U+FFFD for invalid sequences) and percent-encodes non-ASCII in the hop's path, query and fragment, after applying the guard's character rule to the decoded URL (before: UnicodeEncodeError escaped, vector relative-non-ascii-path); a redirect with more than one Location header raises SsrfBlockedError 'Refusing redirect (status N): K Location headers' (before: the first was followed); an empty or blank Location is treated as missing, HTTPError at once (before: the same URL was requested again until the hop cap). Tests: tests/test_redirects.py, vectors/redirect-vectors.json.
